abstained_because: sret_vs_out_param: entry slot 0 is written through a pointer

inferences.claim: the callee pops 4 byte(s) of stack arguments
ECX carries a receiver and is dereferenced before any definite write to it
calling convention is __thiscall: the callee pops the stack arguments, which rules out cdecl and fastcall, and the receiver arrives in ECX
a hidden struct-return pointer is a hypothesis only: entry slot 0 is written through a pointer
in MSVC x86 a hidden struct-return pointer is always stack slot 0 while this is in ECX, so the two never contend
the return value is carried in EAX
the last value written to EAX classifies as integral

sret.basis: entry slot 0 is loaded into a register that is then the base of a write; a hidden struct-return pointer and an out-parameter compile to the same sequence, so the distinction is not decidable from the callee's own listing
